title: Running with Obstacles

exclusion.reason: The original English statement permits any valid RUN/JUMP route. Different valid routes have different output tokens. A scalar feasibility answer or a canonical route would change the original problem, and token comparison would incorrectly reject valid solutions.

sourceAttestedSemantics.inputLayout: Exactly two lines: n m s d, then n distinct obstacle coordinates in arbitrary order.
sourceAttestedSemantics.routeRules: Start at 0 and finish at m. Positive integer RUN/JUMP lengths strictly alternate starting with RUN. Running cannot cross an obstacle. Each JUMP needs the immediately preceding RUN length >= s, has length <= d and must land off obstacles. Never overshoot m and stop immediately at m. Any valid route is allowed.

nonUniqueOutputWitness.explanation: Both routes clear obstacles 3,4 in the first jump and obstacle 7 in the second. Runways are 2 and 1 (s=1), jumps are at most 3, and both land only at non-obstacle coordinates and finish at 10. Output tokens differ at the second jump and final run.

upstreamDiagnostics.scope: Recipe-author diagnostics only, not external-source execution, qualification or independent audit/signoff.
upstreamDiagnostics.method: All 72 official pairs and 2 samples checked against the attested two-line layout, ranges, distinctness and output route rules. For IMPOSSIBLE, a diagnostic greedy groups adjacent obstacles whenever their between-obstacle runway is shorter than s; each forced group requires last-first+2 <= d and the first runway requires firstObstacle-1 >= s. Successful outputs were simulated action by action, not compared with one canonical route. CRLF inputs/outputs were preserved and parsed without rewriting.
upstreamDiagnostics.incompleteness: 26 of the 98 metadata testset entries are absent, and generated_tests is only a count. No completeness claim or generated-basis qualification is made.
